properties.project_name: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P27
properties.digitized_from: Traced as the leftover open ground between DataSF's official street centerlines and neighbouring mapped shapes near the UCSF Medical Center campus, picked by hand by Pier & Point from a numbered map of such leftover pieces, not taken from a surveyed parcel. The chosen piece was then cut further by hand: it forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide); the base was kept and both forks were dropped.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20: the owner corrected the prior resolution (which had P26 'absorbed into the hospital's own footprint, not a separate parcel') using the numbered real-gap-fragment technique. Fragment 49 (a landscaped wedge between the I-280 ramps/curve near 16th St, 3rd St and Owens St, 4,384 sqm raw) forks above a widening base into two thin parallel strips flanking a walkway toward the UCSF building courtyard to the north -- found via a width-cross-section scan (nseg=2 for a wide latitude band, meaning two separate boundary crossings = two parallel arms) rather than eyeballed. Cut at the fork (lat 37.76495, where the cross-section width drops from a single 46m span to two separate ~17m arms) and kept only the single-segment base south of it, per the owner's 'keep the head, drop the horns' instruction. Result: 2,037 sqm triangular landscaped wedge in the freeway-ramp interchange. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: flag, no geometry or identity change (P26/P27 identity is an owner decision). Nothing is cited for the wedge's name, status or use. The polygon sits at about 37.7645 N, 122.393 W, near Owens St and Mariposa St, not at a '16th St/3rd St/Owens St interchange'. OCII's Dec 2015 Attachment B map (page 12) labels P26 as a large parcel at Mariposa St south of blocks 38 and 37, with P27 a thin parcel west of it; in USDA NAIP imagery (viewed 2026-09-29) the polygon traced as this record is a strip of dry grass and bare ground between the I-280 ramp and Owens St, while the polygon traced as P27 (mission_bay_p27_track_field.geojson), east of Owens St, covers a green park. The P26/P27 labels look swapped or misplaced; the owner should compare the map. `status: complete` and `use: park` for this wedge are uncited. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, digitized_from reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/grassed land per Esri satellite imagery and the street/already-tracked-polygon-bounded gap computation, not a surveyed footprint or named park record. Name and operator (likely SFMTA/Caltrans ramp landscaping or an OCII-era open-space installation, matching its P26 plan designation) not confirmed by any source found in this pass.'; digitized_from: 'Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) near the UCSF Medical Center campus. The owner reviewed the numbered fragment map and picked fragment 49 as P26's real extent, then directed a further cut: the fragment forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide) -- keep the base, drop both forks.'. CORRECTED 2026-10-10 (shape truncated; no change to status, use or identity): the owner pointed out that this wedge bulged out over the I-280 ramp lanes. In Esri World Imagery (viewed 2026-10-10) the western part of the old shape lay over marked traffic lanes with vehicles. It is now bounded by the continuation of the two curved edges of the neighbouring Assessor lot 8727008 (The Exchange on 16th) to its north: each edge was extended south-south-east along a circle fitted to the lot's own edge vertices (west edge: radius ~517 m, east edge: ~621 m), and only the part of the old wedge lying between the two extended edges was kept, which narrows it to a triangle that ends where the two edges meet. The top edge still coincides with the lot's south edge (no overlap, no gap). Area 2,033 m2 -> 1,029 m2. The extension is a geometric continuation of the lot lines, not a traced or surveyed boundary. RELABELLED 2026-10-17 (label, name, status, notes, caveat and text; no change to the shape or geometry_type): this record was labelled P26 and is OCII's parcel P27. Read raw 2026-10-17: the Long-Range Property Management Plan for Mission Bay (02 Mission Bay.pdf), Attachment A page 11, row 33 'Park P27 ... Northwest corner of Owens and Mariposa Streets ... 8723-002 ... 15,246' and row 32 'Park P26 ... North side of Mariposa between Owens and 4th Streets ... 8723-003, 004, 006, 007(p) ... 87,556'; OCII's Mission Bay South open-space page lists 'P26 Mariposa Park'. Checked against data/raw/parcels.geojson by location: this outline (1,029 m2) lies 86% inside lot 8723002 (1,457 m2, about 15,683 sq ft against the plan's 15,246) and covers 61% of it, and 0% inside lots 8723003, 8723004, 8723006 and 8723007; the 85%-both-ways rule is not met, so the outline stays drawn, not replaced by the lot. OCII's December 2015 Attachment B map (page 12) also draws P26 as the large parcel on Mariposa St and P27 as a thin parcel west of it. The earlier 'P26' label, the 16th/3rd/Owens interchange description and the guess that this was SFMTA or Caltrans ramp landscaping in the text above are withdrawn: no source supports them. Status changed from 'complete' (which rested only on Pier & Point's own imagery reading, uncited) to 'planned': OCII's September 2023 transition presentation (Item 2 Mission Bay Open Space Transition.pdf, slide 5) lists 'P27 when built' among the parcels Rec and Park will manage, and no later source read says it was built; the 2023-09 milestone moved here from the record that was labelled P27. properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- an outline drawn by hand, traced as the leftover ground between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes; not a surveyed footprint or a parcel line. About 86% of it lies inside Assessor lot 8723002, the lot OCII's Long-Range Property Management Plan names for parcel P27, but it covers only 61% of that lot (1,029 m2 of 1,457 m2), so the lot's own lines are not used. Its west side is cut along the continuation of the curved west edge of the Assessor lot to its north (The Exchange on 16th), because the rest of the earlier shape lay over I-280 ramp lanes; that edge is an extension of the lot line, not a traced boundary. Shown as planned: no source read says the parcel has been built.
properties.notes: OCII plan open-space parcel P27, at the northwest corner of Owens and Mariposa Streets (Assessor lot 8723002). This outline is an approximation of part of that ground.
